subject: DPA follow-up: archival copies, KMS custody, and subprocessor access
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@healthvector.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: DPA follow-up: archival copies & key custody

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Legal had a couple of follow-ups as we map Redwood into our DPA: specifically around archival backups and subprocessor retention. Can you confirm the following so we can finalize the Transfer & Retention appendix?

1) Do archival backups (snapshots and object-store backups) containing customer PII use envelope encryption with keys managed by Redwood KMS, or do we offer a BYOK option for enterprise contracts? If BYOK is available, what formats/algorithms do you support (RSA-OAEP / AES-GCM, key sizes)?

2) Which subprocessors (if any) hold copies of backups for disaster recovery? We only need the subset that could access plaintext under emergency procedures.

3) Retention: what is the default retention period for backups that contain PII, and what’s the process/timeframe for expunging archived copies after a customer retention deletion request?

4) Auditability: can Redwood provide an on-demand export (for HealthVector auditors) of a manifest of backups and the KMS key IDs used to encrypt them? What evidence (logs or signed attestations) do we provide for key rotation events?

We attached our draft transfer appendix and a simplified dataflow diagram — please annotate where backups live and who has key custody. If easier, a short runbook snippet describing emergency unseal/fallback would help.

Requested timeline: we’d like answers by EOD PT Tuesday (3 business days).

Appended files: healthvector_dataflow_diagram_v2.pdf (link also below), draft DPA appendix (docx).

Thanks,
Elena
Legal Ops | HealthVector

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@healthvector.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-30T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up: archival copies & key custody

Hi Elena — appreciate the clear list. Im looping in Aditya (infra/keys) and Jordan (legal) to provide specifics; below is a high-level summary and a draft appendix attached for your review. Ive also annotated the dataflow diagram with preliminary notes (see attachment).

Quick answers:
- Encryption: by default Redwood uses envelope encryption: per-object AES-256-GCM data keys wrapped by a per-tenant KMS key. We do offer BYOK for Dedicated and Private customers; formats supported are AES-256 keys in raw binary (recommended) and RSA-OAEP-wrapped keys for initial import.
- Subprocessors: the primary subprocessor that stores backups is our cloud storage provider (multi-region object store). Access to plaintext is restricted to a small, audited runbook team via an emergency procedure; we can provide a subprocessor list and roles in the appendix.
- Retention & purge: default backup retention is 90 days; cold-archive copies are retained up to 1 year unless a shorter retention is contractually specified. Expungement of archived copies following a deletion request typically completes within 30 days from approval; we have a documented purge playbook.
- Auditability: we can produce a manifest of backup object IDs, associated KMS key IDs, and a signed log excerpt for rotation events. See attached "kms-key-custody-table.csv" for a sample mapping.

Ive attached a draft DPA appendix (dpa-archive-appendix-draft.docx). Jordan / Aditya: please review the technical wording especially around emergency unseal and subprocessors (I tried to be conservative). Elena: if this looks OK I can schedule a follow-up to finalize language.

Best,
Rachel
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa-archive-appendix-draft.docx (draft), kms-key-custody-table.csv (example mapping)

Aditya / Jordan — quick internal note (please reply inline in thread so I can forward back to HealthVector):

- I used the phrase "envelope encryption with per-tenant KMS keys" and offered BYOK for Dedicated/Private. Confirm exact import formats and what well accept for BYOK (PEM-wrapped RSA / raw AES key blobs). HealthVector specifically asked about algorithms.

- For the audit manifest: what fields can we expose without leaking internal metadata? Customer-oriented fields: backup object ID, creation timestamp, KMS key ID, region, retention class. Can we provide signed rotation events (timestamp + key ID + rotation-hash)?

Ill hold on sending a technical response until you confirm. If were able to provide BYOK, Jordan will want a clause about customer key exportability and responsibilities.

Thanks — Rachel

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-01T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: suggested wording + technical gaps for HealthVector

Folks — answers below, happy to be copied back to HealthVector. Long but explicit so legal has everything.

1) Encryption & BYOK
- Default: Envelope encryption with AES-256-GCM per-object data keys. Data keys are generated by the data plane and wrapped with a per-tenant KMS key (AWS KMS-compatible API). Wrapped keys are stored alongside object metadata.
- BYOK: Supported for Dedicated and Private. We accept AES-256 raw key blobs (binary) via our secure import API and RSA key wraps (RSA-OAEP with SHA-256) for import scenarios. Export of a Redwood-managed KMS key is not supported (keys are non-exportable).
- Algorithms: AES-256-GCM for data encryption; RSA-OAEP (SHA-256) for key wrapping on import; HMAC-SHA-256 for integrity checks on manifests.

2) Subprocessors & access to backups
- Subprocessors that hold backups: cloud-object-store-provider (primary), our DR partner (cross-region replication service), and the managed snapshot agent vendor (only for some Dedicated installs).
- Access controls: plaintext access is restricted to a designated "Recovery Operators" group (3 engineers + on-call replacement). Access requires multi-step approval via our Runbook System (ticket + two approvers) and is audited. All actions are logged to an immutable audit stream.

3) Retention & purge timelines
- Default retention: 90 days (hot snapshots), cold-archive retention: up to 365 days. Values are configurable per-tenant for Dedicated/Private customers via account settings or contract.
- Purge process: upon a validated deletion request we trigger a two-phase purge: (a) mark objects for deletion and remove access ACLs, (b) cryptographic shredding / object-store lifecycle rule to physically delete objects. Cold-archive purge completion target: 30 days. We maintain a purge playbook and can provide timestamps/manifest entries evidencing completion.

4) Auditability & evidence
- We can supply: backup object ID, creation timestamp, KMS key ID (Redwood key alias), region, retention-class, and a signed statement of rotation events (timestamp + old-key-id + new-key-id + signature).
- Logs: key usage and key rotation events are available from our KMS audit log; we can provide an extracted, signed log snippet for a given period. Rotation attestations include rotation-hash and operator id.

5) Emergency unseal / runbook
- Emergency access is possible only under: approved incident ticket + two approvers (one infra lead, one security lead) + time-limited credentials. Procedure: retrieve wrapped data key from object metadata, request KMS unwrap via operator-cabinet (requires approval), unwrap returns plaintext data key ephemeral in RAM to decrypt target object. The unwrapped key is never written to persistent storage.

Attachments: Ive attached a sanitized runbook snippet (redwood_kms_unseal_snippet.txt) and an example manifest (kms-key-custody-table.csv).

If Jordan wants stricter contractual language around operator count or attestation frequency, say the word and well tighten.

-Aditya
Principal Engineer, Inference Platform

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@healthvector.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-02T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up: archival copies & key custody (HealthVector)

Hi Elena — thanks for the patience. We reviewed internally and answered each item; summarized below and attached an updated DPA appendix with explicit language you can use in your contract. Key points:

- Encryption: Redwood uses envelope encryption (AES-256-GCM); BYOK available for Dedicated/Private (AES-256 raw import or RSA-OAEP-wrapped import). Redwood-managed KMS keys are non-exportable.
- Subprocessors: cloud-object-store-provider and DR replication partner may hold backups; access to plaintext is limited to a small, auditable Recovery Operators group and requires multi-approver runbook execution.
- Retention & purge: default 90 days / cold-archive up to 365 days; expungement of archived copies after a deletion request targeted at 30 days. Configurable per contract for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Auditability: we can produce backup manifests with KMS key IDs and signed rotation attestations. We will provide a sample manifest and sanitized signed log snippet for your review.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached updated appendix (dpa-archive-appendix-draft.docx, v2) and dataflow annotations.
2) If the BYOK option is required, confirm whether HealthVector prefers raw AES import or RSA-wrapped import; well provide an import checklist and secure upload instructions.
3) If you want operator-count/enforced approval frequency tightened, flag the clause and Jordan will propose firm contractual language.

Would you like a short 30-min call Thursday to walk through the appendix and signoffs? Im available 10–12 PT.

Thanks,
Rachel
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa-archive-appendix-draft.docx (v2), healthvector_dataflow_diagram_v2-annotated.pdf
